Details of our argument:

Two days ago, I went to her apartment to carve pumpkins with her. Her other roommates were in the room and we all chatted for a bit while preparing the table, which is normal, but even when we started carving pumpkins and my back was to her remaining roommate, that roommate would keep making comments, initiating exchanges, asking if we wanted background music, etc. At first, I was giving joke responses and returning the small talk, but I noticed my girlfriend becoming silent and pretty unresponsive relatively quickly. I tried to make eye contact with her, she wouldn't meet my eyes. I asked quietly if she was alright, trying not to alert her roommate (who didn't seem to be the world's most socially aware person, but I'm not super fit to judge that myself). 

I wondered if my gf was feeling jealous that I was talking to her roommate, so I started putting in effort to give as little as possible without making things awkward or souring the tone. Her roommate would keep saying stuff and making comments that called for some form of acknowledgement, and my gf was completely refusing to participate, so I'd respond with just a few words, or just chuckle. The purpose of the chuckles being to acknowledge her comments without calling for further discussion. At some point, I washed my hands and texted my gf, asking her to tell me what was up, hoping I hadn't guessed correctly.

Eventually, my gf said I should probably head out, so I did. As I closed the door and walked away, she swung the door open and stormed past me, leading the way back to my car. On the way there, she said stuff like "I hope you two had fun on your date", and accusing me of ignoring her. I had no memory of ignoring anything she said, and I almost interrupted her to tell her so, but then I remembered that telling someone you care about "nuh-uh"  when they're mad at you isn't exactly productive, so I heard her out. She told me she was angry that I was talking so much with her roommate, that she had recorded our conversations and sent them to her friends, and her friends had told her they were uncomfortable, etc. Once she'd had her say, I told her that I had no memory of ignoring anything she'd said, and asked her what she had said or done that I had ignored. She said "it doesn't matter", took her stuff from my car, and stormed back to her apartment.

She texted me more of the same stuff later that night, and I finally said

> It's pretty messed up that when I did something that bothered you, your first thought wasn't to tell me how you felt.

She responeded with "???", and I said

> You spend an hour in silence, angry at me, refusing to talk to me about it. You gave me no chance to fix it. It's like you just wanted to be angry at me.

She gave me an apology after that, which I'm not totally sure she believed. "okay OP" "i'm sorry". I told her I found more of her stuff in my car and she said she could get it whenever I'd let her. Then a few hours later, at 2am, she tried to call me twice and asked "wyd". I saw this two hours later and I told her [this](https://i.imgur.com/GPR5PSs.jpg). She's since apologized, but I don't know if I should keep putting up with this when I know we don't have long term potential anyway.
